title: Each open of the New project wizard fires 87 requests, which trips the API rate limiter across the whole app
root: Reproduced in the running app. Opening New project fires 87 distinct GET /api/submissions/market-support requests on each full page load. Reopening it inside the same page costs 0, because of the 5-minute module cache. After a reload it costs 87 again. A project page load makes 73 API calls. The fan-out is in client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/AnaVerbs.tsx:80-110 (useFilingOffers): it makes one read per application type in the catalog, then a second round of one read per (type, agency) pair the first round did not name. It has to, because GET /api/submissions/market-support (server/routes/submissions.ts:424-438) accepts only one applicationType, even though readMarketSupport already takes an array of inputs. The report gets the limits wrong. The enterprise-security.ts rateLimiters.api limiter (200/min prod, 2000/min dev) is never mounted. The ceilings that apply are the Redis /api limiter (600/min per credential, server/config/platform-limits.ts:127-133) and the legacy limiter (server/middleware/rateLimiter.ts:96-101, keyed user:<id>, 600/min shared by 11 routers including submissions and QMS, platform-limits.ts:278-283). Because the legacy limiter is keyed per user, two testers signed in as jm.smith share one bucket. That, plus the scripted full reloads that skip the cache, produced the 429 storm. One person reopening the wizard inside the app does not reach 600/min, so 'two opens in a minute exceeds production' is false. The real defect is the 87-request fan-out on every page load. It uses about 15% of a user's per-minute allowance and can exhaust it after a few reloads.
fix: Extend the existing GET /api/submissions/market-support handler (submissions.ts:424) to accept a comma-separated applicationType list, capped (say 100 types). It builds the inputs array and calls readMarketSupport once, returning { byType: { [type]: markets[] } }, while still answering the single-type shape as today. In AnaVerbs.tsx useFilingOffers, make one batched read for the first round and one batched read for the unnamed (type, agency) pairs, through the existing readOffer cache (key: the batched path). marketSupportPath in MarketSupportLine.tsx gains an array overload. No new route, service or table.
test: client/src/concept2cure/v2/__tests__/registryPickerOffers.test.tsx: mount RegistryPicker with the full catalog and assert reads() (the existing counter at line 399) is at most 2 on first mount. Today it is one per application type plus the second round.
observed: The limiter is keyed per IP and the other tester shares that address. Soon every call returns HTTP 429 Too Many Requests, including /api/c2c/projects, /api/module-subscriptions/navigation, /api/chat/threads and /api/organizations/2. The wizard then shows 'Which filing types the platform can carry could not be read, so none is offered yet. Retry' and no filing can be chosen. Recents shows 'Couldn’t load your conversations.' On a project's Review step, Open CAPAs, change controls and nonconforming product all read 'Could not be read' (429 on /api/mdx/qms/documents?program_id=…). The dev limit is 2000 requests/min (enterprise-security.ts: api max 200*10). The production limit is 200/min per IP, so in production one user opening the wizard twice in a minute would exceed it.

title: Every project's data room lists other clients' quality records (Lumen, MDX), including a brand-new project and the C2C-101 demo
root: Reproduced by API: project 6bd3d04c (and C2C-101) GET /sources returns 21 native_record_snapshot rows with sourceScope 'organization'. They come from three causes. (a) By design: server/services/qms/project-evidence.ts:117 ('One admitted project plus explicitly labelled organization QA/QS context') adds organization-wide Quality registers to every project. qms_suppliers, qms_internal_audits and qms_management_reviews (project-evidence.ts:62-66; project-evidence-queries.ts) have no client_workspace_id or program_id column. (b) Data: the Lumen demo pack (scripts/demo/launch-demo/packs/lumen-qms-content.mjs) writes its four clinical deviations into qc_deviations with client_workspace_id NULL. The query admits NULL-workspace rows into every workspace (project-evidence-queries.ts qc_deviations). (c) Data: the NP-100 and C2C-101 change controls were created with program_id NULL, so the 'optional-project' query (program_id IS NULL OR = project) admits them everywhere. Commit 5f8eabad1 fixes this for creation only; the existing local rows keep NULL. All of these 'clients' are fictional demo sponsors seeded into one organization; in a real deployment each sponsor is its own tenant. The 'Data Room sources · 0' vs 21 mismatch did not reproduce. GET /records for 6bd3d04c now counts 21 sources: /records counts the same client_document rows (server/routes/c2c/projects.ts:1544-1548). The 0 was read before the Evidence step's GET /sources ran syncQualityProjectSources (record-source.ts:96), which writes the snapshots on the first catalogue read. Whether organization-wide QMS registers should be scoped per client workspace in a multi-client organization would need a new column, so it is a founder decision, not a session fix.
fix: DATA: in lumen-qms-content.mjs, create the Lumen deviations with Lumen's client_workspace_id, creation-only, as 5f8eabad1 did for change controls. Then they no longer surface in Concept2Cure Therapeutics projects. For this local database, re-seed or set client_workspace_id and program_id on the demo rows. Suppliers, audits and management reviews stay organization context unless the founder decides to scope them per client workspace.
test: Demo-pack check (scripts/demo tests): every qc_deviations row the Lumen pack writes carries the Lumen client_workspace_id, and GET /api/c2c/projects/<C2C-101>/sources lists no qc_deviations row titled '[Demo · Lumen]'.
observed: The brand-new, empty project shows 'Data room 21 sources · 21 readable on this page'. The list includes 'Supplier: [Demo · Lumen] Quorvex IRT Systems', 'Management review: Lumen 2026-Q2', 'Internal audit: LMN-IA-2027-01', 'Change control: [Demo · MDX] NP-100 software v2.3.0 …' and 'GMP deviation: [Demo · Lumen] Site 105 …', all origin native_record_snapshot. Each row says 'The original file is unavailable, so a working copy cannot be created.' The same 21 rows appear in the C2C-101 demo project and in an EU project. The same page's Records card says 'Data Room sources · 0', which contradicts the count of 21.

title: Priority Review, PMR/PMC, SUPAC, 15-Day Alert Report (ICSR) and Environmental Assessment are created as full NDA marketing projects
root: Reproduced by API on project 1070ffc5 ('15-Day Alert Report (ICSR)'): program_type 'nda', submission 26 with application_type 'nda', and filing document 'C2C-101 — NDA × FDA · 505(b)(1) · eCTD M1–M5'. Cause: a catalog entry with no pathwayKey is given pathway 'ctd' in client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/Projects.tsx:453 and :705 (`pathway: ctx.pathwayKey || 'ctd'`). programTypeFor then returns 'nda' at Projects.tsx:181 (`pw === 'ctd'`). us_icsr_15day, us_pmr, us_supac, us_ea and us_priority_review have no PATHWAY_BY_ID entry (shared/regulatory/filing-catalog.ts:123-158) and no FILING_DOCUMENT_CLASSES entry (shared/regulatory/filing-document-classes.ts:59-117). So the market verdict is asked about NDA|FDA, which is build_and_sequence with appliesTo [US_351K, US_505B2, US_ACCEL_APPROVAL, US_ANDA, US_BLA, US_NDA, US_ROLLING]. The picker shows them as 'unclaimed' ('No tier is stated… opens a project whose application type is NDA') but still lets the user create them. PATHWAY_BY_ID's own comment says unmapped filings should fail closed rather than be filed as a US NDA. The wizard's 'ctd' default defeats that.
fix: Remove the `|| 'ctd'` default at Projects.tsx:453 and :705. In programTypeFor, when the entry has no pathwayKey and no document class, return the filing id lowercased (an unmapped application type) instead of reaching the 'nda' or 'ind' fallbacks. GET market-support then answers through unmappedSupport (not offered: no filing outline). The picker lists the filing under Not offered and POST refuses it, since it is not in VALID_PROGRAM_TYPES. Keep the filings that really are NDAs by adding explicit 'ctd' entries to PATHWAY_BY_ID for us_accel_approval and us_rolling (they are in the NDA appliesTo). Mapping ICSR, PMR, SUPAC, EA and Priority Review to their own classes needs rule packs, which is a founder decision.
test: client/src/concept2cure/v2/__tests__/registryPickerOffers.test.tsx: for each catalog entry whose programTypeFor result is 'nda', assert its id is in the NDA offer's appliesTo. Assert '15-Day Alert Report (ICSR)', 'Priority Review', 'SUPAC Supplement', 'Post-Marketing Requirement (PMR) / PMC' and 'Environmental Assessment (EA)' appear under Not offered and are not selectable.
observed: The wizard says 'No tier is stated for this filing… Creating it opens a project whose application type is NDA.' The review page reads 'Recorded as NDA · Drug'. The POST sends programType 'nda' with submissionTypeId us_icsr_15day, us_priority_review, us_pmr, us_supac or us_ea. The project header reads 'NDA · FDA'. About shows 'NDA number not assigned' and 'Client type Pharma'. Submit offers 'NDA · FDA (US)'. A 15-day safety report is scaffolded as a full NDA dossier, and for a biologic sponsor a PMR or SUPAC should not be an NDA at all.

title: The picker's 'Not offered' reasons name the wrong application ('no governed NDA outline') for EU, Canadian, Australian and Korean filings that are not NDAs
root: Reproduced: GET market-support?applicationType=nda&market=EMA returns 'EMA has no governed NDA outline here…', and the same NDA wording comes back for Health Canada. The root cause is the same as #2. EU variations, PIP, orphan, RMP, renewal, scientific advice, PRIME, CMA, accelerated assessment, ca_cta_a, au_cta, kr_* and the other JP ids have no PATHWAY_BY_ID entry (shared/regulatory/filing-catalog.ts:123-158). The wizard defaults their pathway to 'ctd' (Projects.tsx:705), programTypeFor maps that to 'nda' (Projects.tsx:181), and the picker asks the verdict about NDA|<agency>. notOfferedReason (server/services/regulatory/market-support.ts:204) names the application type it was asked about ('NDA'), not the filing chosen. Ids that are mapped (ca_cta, au_ctn and jp_ctn to 'cta') correctly read 'no governed CTA outline'.
fix: The same change as #2: an unmapped filing resolves to its own id, not 'nda'. GET market-support then answers through unmappedSupport (market-support.ts:426-450), and the reason names that filing's type ('no filing outline for the application type eu_variation_ii'). The picker can show it with the entry's displayName, through the existing reasonByFiling/own-reason path in AnaVerbs.tsx. No reason names NDA for a filing that is not an NDA.
test: client/src/concept2cure/v2/__tests__/registryPickerOffers.test.tsx: no Not-offered reason for an entry whose agency is EMA, Health Canada, TGA, MFDS or PMDA contains 'NDA', unless the entry is itself an NDA-family filing.

EMA has no governed NDA outline here, so a project would have nothing to author…' The same NDA wording appears for Type IB/II Variation, Paediatric Investigation Plan, Orphan Drug Designation (EMA), Risk Management Plan, Renewal, Scientific Advice, PRIME, Conditional MA and Accelerated Assessment. It also appears for 'Clinical Trial Application Amendment · Health Canada', 'Pre-submission Meeting (Health Canada)', 'Clinical Trial Approval (Australia) · TGA', 'IND Application (South Korea) · MFDS', 'Pre-application Consultation (PMDA)' and 'Sakigake Designation'. title: The server accepts a filing the picker marks not offered: an EU Type II variation becomes a full MAA project
root: Classified from code reading. I did not repeat the POST, to avoid creating more projects. In server/routes/c2c/projects.ts:813-862 the pre-write gate builds MarketInput from body.programType and primaryAgency only, and calls marketOfferGivenOutline. submissionTypeId (line 818) is recorded but never checked against the application type the catalog gives it. So any API caller can send submissionTypeId 'eu_variation_ii' with programType 'maa', pass the MAA|EMA offer, and get a full MAA scaffold, even though the picker (which derives the type from the filing) lists the variation as not offered. The UI cannot produce this; only a direct API call can.
fix: Move programTypeFor (Projects.tsx:122) unchanged into shared/regulatory/filing-catalog.ts, beside PATHWAY_BY_ID, and import it from Projects.tsx. That is a move, not new code. In POST /api/c2c/projects, when submissionTypeId resolves to a catalog entry (resolveFilingCatalogEntry), compute its application type with the shared function. Refuse with 422 FILING_NOT_OFFERED when it differs from body.programType, or when that type's offer is not_offered.
test: server/routes/c2c __tests__ for POST /api/c2c/projects: body { submissionTypeId: 'eu_variation_ii', programType: 'maa', primaryAgency: 'EMA' } returns 422 FILING_NOT_OFFERED and writes no regulatory_programs row.
observed: The server returns 201 and creates project 6bd3d04c-819a-438c-a245-73738cb40a05 with program_type 'maa' and submissionTypeId 'eu_variation_ii'. The picker lists 'Type II Variation (Major) · EMA' as not offered. The server's check is keyed on programType plus agency and ignores the filing id.

title: Japan Clinical Trial Notification: the picker and the server give different refusal reasons, and the server's reason is wrong for a CTN
root: The picker's reason is reproduced by API: GET market-support?applicationType=cta&market=PMDA returns 'PMDA has no governed CTA outline here…'. The server's different reason follows from code. POST's pre-write gate (server/routes/c2c/projects.ts:861) calls marketOfferGivenOutline(input, true), which assumes an outline exists. That skips the outline refusal, and notOfferedReason then reaches the PMDA v4.0 branch (server/services/regulatory/market-support.ts:208-212), returning 'PMDA requires eCTD v4.0 for new applications'. That branch applies to every non-device type, including 'cta'. Device filings are exempt (market-support.ts:690), but a clinical trial notification is not an eCTD marketing application either. So the two verdicts disagree, and the server's reason is wrong for a CTN.
fix: In market-support.ts, apply pmdaBlocked only to marketing application types: pass false for 'cta', as the device branch does at line 690. POST then passes the pre-write gate, the scaffold finds no PMDA cta pack, and the post-scaffold check (projects.ts:1095-1097) refuses with the same 'no governed CTA outline' reason the picker shows. server/services/regulatory has no owning package in one-design-plan.json (S5's glob is the root services/regulatory/**), so only F1 covers it.
test: server/services/regulatory/__tests__/market-support.test.ts: marketOfferGivenOutline({ applicationType: 'cta', market: 'PMDA' }, true) is not refused with the eCTD v4.0 reason. marketOfferGivenOutline({ applicationType: 'cta', market: 'PMDA' }, false).reason equals the GET verdict's reason for cta|PMDA.
observed: The picker says 'PMDA has no governed CTA outline here…'. The server answers 422 'PMDA requires eCTD v4.0 for new applications, and this platform builds eCTD v3.2.2 only.' A clinical trial notification is not an eCTD marketing application.

title: The client type is derived from the filing, not the client, which mislabels biotech projects and hides DMF projects from the filter
root: Reproduced by API: the project list returns ws counts { Biotech: 62, Pharma: 15, MDX: 2, Dmf: 2 }. shared/constants/domain/product-types.ts:297-300 (WORKSTREAM_FILING_TYPES) has no 'dmf'. workstreamSqlCase therefore falls to `ELSE initcap(replace(col,'_',' '))` (product-types.ts:351) and returns 'Dmf'. ProjectPortfolioFilters.tsx:60 (CLIENT_TYPES) offers only MDX, Biotech and Pharma, so the DMF rows match no option and the per-option totals do not add up to 'All'. On ProjectHome.tsx:1913, workstreamForFilingType('dmf') returns null, so About reads 'not recorded'. The 'Pharma' label for a biotech client's NDA, CTA or MAA is the existing design: the workstream is derived from the filing type (WORKSTREAM_FILING_TYPES: Pharma = nda, maa, jnda, anda, cta), and Projects.tsx:1032 derives it the same way on purpose. Renaming 'Client type' or deriving it from the client workspace instead would be a founder decision. The DMF gap is a plain defect.
fix: In product-types.ts, bucket 'dmf' by its stated product class, as filing document classes are (a DMF covers drugs and biologics, P-21). Add 'dmf' to the types handled by WORKSTREAM_BY_PRODUCT_CLASS, both in workstreamForFilingType and in workstreamSqlCase's classBranch. Every DMF row then lands in Biotech or Pharma and the filter totals add up. No UI change is needed once the server stops returning 'Dmf'.
test: shared/constants/domain __tests__ (product-types): workstreamForFilingType('dmf','drug') === 'Pharma' and ('dmf','biologic') === 'Biotech'. For every VALID_PROGRAM_TYPES value with a product class, workstreamSqlCase produces one of MDX, Biotech or Pharma, never the initcap echo.
observed: The wizard review and About card say 'Client type Pharma' for NDA, CTA and MAA projects. DMF projects are stored with ws 'Dmf' and About shows 'Client type not recorded'. The Projects filter reads 'All client types (70)' but its options add up to 68 (Medical device & IVD 1, Biotech 53, Pharma 14), so the two DMF projects cannot be reached through it. A biotech user filtering 'Biotech' loses their own EU CTA or MAA.

title: Project headers show raw or inconsistent filing labels
root: Classified from code reading (minor). The header's filing words come from ProjectHome.tsx:2130 (`filingTypeWords(prog?.program_type) ?? filingDocumentClassOf(...)?.label`), which calls programTypeLabel (client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/programSequence.ts:208-212). That returns the SC_APPTYPES label (client/src/concept2cure/v2/fixtures/submission.ts:41-51: ind, nda, bla, anda, maa, 510k, de_novo, pma, cta only). Otherwise it returns the document class's sentence-case label ('clinical study report', 'IND amendment'), or the raw value ('dmf'). A capitalising labeller already exists: Projects.tsx filingLabel/documentClassLabel (Projects.tsx:186-205) gives 'Clinical study report', 'IND amendment' and 'DMF'.

title: Internal section codes (snake_case and ':work:N') leak into the outline, the canvas, toasts, AnA buttons and the exported Word headings
root: Reproduced in the running app and in the exports. The C2C-101 CSR outline rows read 'm5.3.5.1:work:1 1 Title Page'. After clicking '2 Synopsis', the canvas eyebrow (.ed-mast-num) reads 'm5.3.5.1:work:2'. The CSR, 1571 and IB .docx files have headings 'm5.3.5.1:work:N', '1.1.1:work:N', 'title_page' and 'table_of_contents'. Two causes. (1) shared/regulatory/section-code.ts:285-288 `sectionNumberLabel` hides only snake_case named-matter codes. It does not recognise the document-local working codes minted at server/services/authoring/ind-template-outlines-m1.ts:33 (`${code}:work:${i}`), ind-template-outlines-m4-m5.ts:18 (`${section.code}:work:${ordinal}`) and ind-authoring-templates.ts:73 (`work:sap:`), so the outline (DocumentWorkbench.tsx:4664) and the eyebrow (5284) print them. (2) Several display sites print the raw code with no label helper at all: the save toast at DocumentWorkbench.tsx:3577-3578 ('Section saved (table_of_contents)'); the AnA bridge, which passes section.code at DocumentWorkbench.tsx:1317 and prints it at ConversationThread.tsx:293-294, 303 and 309-310; the Word heading and REF text at server/export/authoring-blocks-to-docx.ts:228-237 (`targetSegments` pushes the raw code, so the heading reads '<code> - <title>'); and shared/authoring/cross-references.ts:105-113 `crossReferenceText`. Snake_case codes are already hidden in the outline by the J3 fix; only the other sites leak them.
fix: Leave the stored codes alone: they are section identity, and seeded rows would only drift. (1) Extend `sectionNumberLabel` so it also returns '' for working codes: /:work:\d+$/i and /^work:/i. (2) Route every display site through it and fall back to the title when it returns ''. That means the toast at DocumentWorkbench.tsx:3577-3578 and the bridge at :1317 (pass a `sectionLabel` = sectionNumberLabel(code) || title, which ConversationThread prints in place of `bridge.sectionCode`). It also means `targetSegments` in authoring-blocks-to-docx.ts:233 and `crossReferenceText` in shared/authoring/cross-references.ts:109, so the heading and the REF fields stay in step: code display already falls back to the title when there is no code. No new helper is needed.

The canvas eyebrow above the section title is 'm5.3.5.1:work:2'. The save toast says 'Section saved (table_of_contents) — open History…'. AnA's button reads 'Insert into m5.3.5.1:work:1 as tracked suggestion' or 'Insert into executive_summary as tracked suggestion'. Exported Word headings read 'title_page - Title Page', 'confidentiality_statement - Confidentiality Statement', 'table_of_contents - Table of Contents', 'executive_summary - Executive Summary', 'm5.3.5.1:work:1 - 1 Title Page' and '1.1.1:work:1 - Name, address, and telephone of sponsor'.

title: A freshly created template document warns that its sections are stored out of order
root: Reproduced for the CSR (5.3.5.1, 120 sections) and the Form 1571 worksheet (1.1.1, 10 working rows): GET /api/authoring/docs/:id/sections returns structure.outOfOrder=true, and the editor shows the warning. NOT reproduced for the 1.2 Cover Letter: it has only 9 working rows, outOfOrder is false and no warning appears. The stored order is correct (order_index 0..119). The comparator is wrong. shared/regulatory/section-code.ts:55-63 `segments()` splits only on '.', so 'm5.3.5.1:work:10' yields a last segment '1:WORK:10'. `compareSegment` (line 79) compares that as text, so 'work:10' sorts before 'work:2' as soon as a document has 10 or more working rows. `sectionStructureIssues` (line 249) is computed with this comparator at server/services/authoring/authoring-document-read.ts:168. Its suggestedOrder is scrambled too (work:1, work:10, work:100, work:101 ...), so a 'repair' would wreck the CSR. `sectionInsertSlot` uses the same comparator, so a section added to a CSR would be stored in the wrong place.
fix: In `segments()`, before splitting, normalise the base through the existing `normalizeCtdCode` (which strips the leading 'm'), split off a /:work:(\d+)$/i suffix, and append it as a trailing numeric segment. 'm5.3.5.1:work:10' then compares as [5,3,5,1,10]: after its parent 5.3.5.1, and numerically among its siblings. Everything that uses `compareSectionCode` picks this up (structure check, insert slot, sort).
test: shared/regulatory/__tests__/section-code.test.ts: sectionStructureIssues(['5.3.5.1', ...Array.from({length:12}, (_, i) => `m5.3.5.1:work:${i+1}`)]).outOfOrder === false, and the same with '1.1.1' plus '1.1.1:work:1..10'. This fails today.
observed: Right after creation, with no edits, the outline shows: 'These sections are stored in an order that differs from their section codes, and they assemble and export in the stored order. Reorder them if the stored order is not deliberate.' The ':work:N' child codes do not sort numerically against the parent code (for example '5.3.5.1' against 'm5.3.5.1:work:1'), so the template's own order is flagged.

title: The main demo project has no clinical source, so the CSR 'Build from the study's data' flow cannot be shown on C2C-101
root: Reproduced: GET /api/submission-orchestrator/csr/sources?programId=6065271c-… returns {sources:[], unreadable:[], limitReached:false}. The empty state in StudyDataBuild/StudyDataSource is honest and correct. The biotech demo pack (scripts/demo/launch-demo/packs/biotech*.mjs) seeds no clinical source for C2C-101. The synthetic `concept2cure.csr-source.v1` sources are seeded only by the portfolio pack, for studies past database lock (scripts/demo/launch-demo/packs/portfolio.mjs:40, :288, :570). C2C-101's own seeded milestone puts its CSR at +630 days (biotech-content.mjs:387), so a study-data source on this IND-stage project would contradict the demo's own timeline. This is a demo-script and data choice, not a code fault.

title: The revision count beside the section does not update after a save until the page is reloaded
root: Reproduced by API on 'Sweep Pre-IND Briefing Document C2C-101'. The PATCH /api/authoring/sections/:id answered 200 with revision_created=true, but the returned `section` had no revision_count key. The GET that followed showed revision_count 3 (it was 2 before). The cause is at server/routes/authoring.router.ts:1811-1815: the update does `RETURNING *` from authoring_sections, which has no revision_count column (it is computed only in the read at server/services/authoring/authoring-document-read.ts:150), and lines 2096-2098 return that row. The client merges `{...s, ...adopted}` at DocumentWorkbench.tsx:3555-3559, so the stale count survives in the meta line (5348-5349). The toast at 3576-3578 always falls back to 'Section saved (code) — open History to confirm the revision', which is also the toast wording quoted in defect #0. Client tests mock revision_count in the PATCH response, so they pass even though the server never sends it.
fix: Inside the PATCH transaction, after the revision insert and before COMMIT, read `SELECT COUNT(*)::int AS revision_count FROM doc_revisions WHERE section_id=$1 AND tenant_id=$2` on the same client. That is the same expression as authoring-document-read.ts:150. Return `section: { ...result.rows[0], revision_count }`. The client already adopts it, so no client change is needed.

title: Read endpoints intermittently return 503 during editor use (sources and AnA activity)
root: Not reproduced at rest: all six endpoints returned 200 (section sources, project sources, agent-activity, the team view, live-drive/state). Under a 120-request concurrent burst from one session, project sources returned 15 × 503 {error:'PROJECT_ACCESS_UNAVAILABLE', message:'Current project access could not be verified. No project data was supplied.'}, 4 × 500 and 2 × 401. Section sources and the ana-ri routes stayed at 200, except for one 500. These 503s are deliberate fail-closed refusals, with honest wording, raised when the access check cannot reach the database under pool contention: server/services/data-room-retrieval.ts:76, server/middleware/auth.ts:236 SESSION_UNCHECKED, orgMembership.ts:362, tenantContext.ts:219. They are not gated on the AI gateway. The editor's Sources loader already separates 'error' from an empty list (DocumentWorkbench.tsx:3150-3151), so a failed read is not shown as empty. Separate real defect found under the same load, and worth a fix: server/auth.ts:352-354 is a catch-all that answers 401 'Invalid or expired token' when the membership query throws (for example a pool timeout). The client treats that as signed out, so a database hiccup logs the user out. It should answer 503, as middleware/auth.ts:236 already does.
fix: The reported behaviour needs no change. For the separate defect: in server/auth.ts's authenticate catch, answer 503 {code:'SESSION_UNCHECKED', message:'The session could not be checked. Try again.'} for a database or infrastructure error, matching middleware/auth.ts:236. Keep 401 for JWT verification failures only.

root: The eviction is environment-only: one demo account is shared, DEFAULT_MAX_CONCURRENT_SESSIONS is 5 (shared/auth/session-policy.ts:6), and every dev-login opens a session. Sign in again.'} after other testers signed in, and I had to sign in a second time. Nothing was created.` around a server sentence that already ends in '.'. The same pattern is at client/src/concept2cure/v2/authoringHandoff.ts:138.
fix: Strip trailing sentence punctuation from the redacted server message before inserting it, the same way IndLifecycle.tsx:371 already does: redactInternals(...).replace(/[.!?]\s*$/, ''). title: Freeze and E-sign cannot be completed: the dev user's password is unknown in this environment
root: I confirmed this from config and DB state. I did not type a password, to avoid locking the account. server/db/bootstrap/seed-default-org.ts:76-91 resolveDemoPasswordHash() hashes a random, discarded password when DEMO_USER_PASSWORD is unset, and .env does not set it. The users row for id 1 was created 2026-11-08 22:16:38 with that hash. The seed's ON CONFLICT never overwrites an existing hash (comment at seed-default-org.ts:70-74), so setting the variable now changes nothing without a rotation. The UI is honest: verify-password answers 200 {valid:false}. An urgent related demo risk: users.failed_login_attempts for jm.smith is already 4. LOCKOUT_THRESHOLD is 5 and the lockout lasts 30 minutes (server/services/auth-security-service.ts:30-31), and /api/esignature/verify-password counts each wrong password against that lockout (server/routes/esignature.ts:80-96). One more wrong password during the demo locks the presenter out of every signing act (HTTP 423 ACCOUNT_LOCKED).
fix: Operator action, no code: set DEMO_USER_PASSWORD (operator-held) and rotate the existing jm.smith hash to it, because the seed never overwrites an existing row. Reset failed_login_attempts/locked_until for user 1 before the demo. Check whether signing then asks for MFA (verify-password returns mfaRequired), and have the second factor ready.

The UI is honest, but no password can work: seed-default-org.ts hashes a random, discarded password when DEMO_USER_PASSWORD is unset, and .env does not set it. title: Place into filing in the editor refuses the right CTD code for any document made from an IND template whose sections are coded ':work:N'
root: Reproduced in the running app. I opened /concept2cure/document-authoring?program=6065…&documentId=dc4dcd8f-…&sectionCode=1.20:work:1 and clicked Place into filing. Section code is prefilled '1.20:work:1' and refused at once: '"1.20:work:1" is not a CTD section code…'. The template outline mints working headings as `${code}:work:${i+1}` and marks them 'Working preparation heading, not an additional CTD node' (server/services/authoring/ind-template-outlines-m1.ts:33-35; the m2-m3 and m4-m5 outlines do the same). In client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/AuthoringPlaceIntoFiling.tsx:119-121, documentFilingCode() runs every code through normalizeCtdCode, whose CTD_CODE regex rejects ':work:N' (shared/regulatory/section-code.ts:85, 115-121). It returns null whenever any code fails ('codes.length !== sectionCodes.length'). With ownCode null, openDialog (line 249) falls back to activeSectionCode '1.20:work:1', which judgeSectionCode cannot place. Typing 1.20 is then refused by ownSectionRefusal (lines 137-147): own is null and 1.20 is one of the document's own section codes. Every template scaffold with ':work:' rows, including 1.2 Cover Letter and Form 1571, can never be placed from the editor.
fix: In AuthoringPlaceIntoFiling.tsx, read a working heading as the CTD node it prepares. Add a local `filingNodeOf = (c) => normalizeCtdCode(String(c ?? '').replace(/:work:\d+$/, ''))` and use it in documentFilingCode (line 120) and in ownSectionRefusal's membership test (line 141). For the 1.20 template the codes all resolve to 1.20, so ownCode = '1.20' is prefilled and accepted. Nothing new on the server: the Vault path already files at 1.20. Possible follow-up, outside this fix: the server's filingSectionMembers (server/services/c2c/filing-section-target.ts:39-41) and filingSectionKey (shared/regulatory/filing-section-key.ts:20-27) match only '<key>.' children, so a save of a ':work:' section does not reach node 1.20 either.
test: documentAuthoringPlaceIntoFiling.test.tsx: documentFilingCode(['1.20','1.20:work:1',…,'1.20:work:9']) === '1.20', and ownSectionRefusal('1.20', same codes) === null. Render the dialog with activeSectionCode '1.20:work:1' and those sectionCodes, and assert the Section code input is prefilled '1.20' with no 'not a CTD section code' note.
observed: The section code is prefilled with '1.20:work:1', which the dialog immediately rejects: '"1.20:work:1" is not a CTD section code. Use one like 1.2, 2.7.3 or 3.2.S.4.2.' Entering 1.20 is also refused: '1.20 is one section of this document. Placement files the whole saved document (10 sections) as one leaf, so it is filed at the document's own code — a code that covers all of its sections.' No code is suggested and 'Place leaf in the sequence' stays disabled. The document cannot be placed at 1.20 from the editor, so 'Re-file saved text' can never become available for it. Workaround: File to vault, then Vault > Place into filing at 1.20, which works.

root: Not reproduced. The Evidence step stacks three things, in this order: DataRoom, ProjectProtocol, then ProjectEvidence ('Project files', ProjectHome.tsx:2211-2220). title: Revision history shows raw HTML, omits the reason for change, and adding a comment creates a content revision
root:
Reproduced in the running app: the Versions rail shows '

C2C-101 … humanized IgG1…' and gives every card the origin label 'edited', with no reason. There are two causes. (1) DocumentWorkbench.tsx:5906 renders `(r.content ?? '').slice(0, 400)` as a text node, so the stored HTML shows as markup. The visible-text helper the diff already uses exists as visibleText in editor/textDiff.ts:23 but is not exported. (2) The reason for change is not stored on doc_revisions, whose columns are id, section_id, content, created_by, tenant_id, created_at, content_sha256, prev_chain_sha256, chain_sha256, origin and inputs. GET /api/authoring/sections/:id/history (server/routes/authoring.router.ts:2119-2150) therefore returns none, and AuthRevision (DocumentWorkbench.tsx:239-250) has no field for one. The reason is in authoring_audit_trail.change_reason, and its content_hash_after equals doc_revisions.content_sha256. For this section, f9b1660d…='Initial drug name statement for sweep test' and b22eebec…='Comment anchor applied'. The comment-anchor revision itself is deliberate: the anchor lives in the section HTML and is saved under a system reason (RichSectionEditor.tsx:1515-1521). It reads as an unexplained edit only because the card shows neither the reason nor the visible text.
fix: Server, history query at authoring.router.ts:2125: add `LEFT JOIN LATERAL (SELECT change_reason FROM authoring_audit_trail a WHERE a.section_id = r.section_id AND a.tenant_id = r.tenant_id AND a.content_hash_after = r.content_sha256 ORDER BY a.created_at DESC LIMIT 1) ar ON TRUE` and select ar.change_reason AS reason. This uses an existing table; nothing new. Client: export visibleText from textDiff.ts. In the revision card, render visibleText(r.content).slice(0, 400), add `reason?: string|null` to AuthRevision, and show 'Reason: …' beside the origin. 'Comment anchor applied' then labels the anchor revision as what it is.
test:
Client test (e.g. authoringAnaPane/workbench history test): mock /history to return content '

a b

' with reason 'Comment anchor applied'. Expect card text 'a b' and 'Comment anchor applied', and no '
observed:
Each revision card shows markup, e.g. '

C2C-101 (established name pending USAN) is a humanized IgG1 …'. The saved reason ('Initial drug name statement for sweep test') is not shown on the card; only the Audit trail has it. Adding a comment produced a new revision v3 ('Comment anchor applied' in the audit trail). The header jumped from v2 to v3 with no edit by the user, and 'What changed' says only 'only markup or formatting moved'.

title: Revision count and version are stale right after Save
root: Confirmed by code reading. revision_count is not a column of authoring_sections. It is computed only by the document read (server/services/authoring/authoring-document-read.ts:150, COUNT over doc_revisions). The section save PATCH /api/authoring/sections/:sectionId ends `UPDATE authoring_sections … RETURNING *` (authoring.router.ts:1811-1816) and responds with section: result.rows[0] (line 2098), which has no revision_count. The client merges `{ ...s, ...(adopted ?? {}) }` (DocumentWorkbench.tsx:3558), so the old count survives. The header 'v{revs}' (line 4727) and the meta line (5348-5349) stay stale until a reload. The save toast falls back to 'open History to confirm the revision' (3576-3578) for the same reason.
fix: In the PATCH route, inside the same transaction after the revision insert, read `SELECT COUNT(*)::int AS revision_count FROM doc_revisions WHERE section_id=$1 AND tenant_id=$2` and respond with section: { ...result.rows[0], revision_count }. The client already adopts that key, and the existing toast will then say 'revision N recorded'. Client-only alternative: when json.revision_created is true and adopted.revision_count is absent, set revision_count = num(s.revision_count) + 1.

Client test in authoringSaveFilingCommit.test.tsx: after a mocked save that returns revision_count 2, the ed-versions button reads 'v2'.

title: 'Assemble a test package' returns HTTP 500 'Request failed' and swallows a valid FDA 1789 refusal
root: Reproduced by API on 2026-11-09. POST /api/submissions/sequences/1/assemble returned 500 {code:INTERNAL,'Request failed.'} with correlationId 29919aa7-8795-4648-a54f-51342747e2e1. The dev log line for that id holds the real refusal: 'FDA validation 1789 (technical rejection): 2 file(s) in Module 4/5 study sections ... protoco-vault-documents-e7ae5774-....pdf (section m5.3.5.1, no study id); sap-sta-vault-documents-dc4f5bfc-....pdf ...', code null. The packager throws a plain ValidationError (server/services/submission-gateways/types.ts:586, no `code`) at server/services/submission-gateways/regional-packager.ts:1066. assembleSequence converts only FdaSubmissionIdentityRefusal into EctdAssemblyBlockedError (server/services/ectd/assemble-from-core.ts:343-350, the .catch on packageSequenceFromCore) and lets the ValidationError through. The route catch (server/routes/submissions.ts:2056-2066) maps only EctdAssemblyBlockedError to 422. fail() (:136-198) has no CODE_STATUS entry for a code-less error, so it answers 500. The governed freeze/dispatch path does not have this problem: submission-service.ts:1888-1893 wraps any assembly error as DISPATCH_BLOCKED. Only the dry-run assemble route leaks it. The client panel (SequenceAssembleTestPackage.tsx:134-138) already shows a 422 refusal's text, so the fix is server-only.
fix: In assemble-from-core.ts, widen the existing .catch on packageSequenceFromCore (around :343) so that a packager ValidationError (import from ../submission-gateways/types) is treated like FdaSubmissionIdentityRefusal. It records an ECTD_ASSEMBLE_BLOCKED audit row with details {reason:'packager_validation', findings: err.findings} and rethrows new EctdAssemblyBlockedError(err.message, auditTrail). The route's existing 422 ECTD_ASSEMBLE_BLOCKED branch then carries the 1789 sentence and the audit outcome to the test-package panel. No route or client change is needed.

Expect POST /sequences/:id/assemble to return 422 with error.code ECTD_ASSEMBLE_BLOCKED and a message containing 'FDA validation 1789', plus an ECTD_ASSEMBLE_BLOCKED audit row. Today it returns 500 INTERNAL.

The UI says: 'Whether the test package was assembled could not be confirmed — Request failed. Check the sequence's audit trail before assembling again.' The dev log for correlationId b096c48f-9b75-44ed-83be-a8e8aac3ea0f shows the real cause, a deliberate refusal: 'FDA validation 1789 (technical rejection): 2 file(s) in Module 4/5 study sections would be referenced by no Study Tagging File — protoco-vault-documents-e7ae5774-….pdf (section m5.3.5.1, no study id); sap-sta-vault-documents-dc4f5bfc-….pdf (section m5.3.5.1, no study id). Give each its study id and STF file-tag, or file it under 4.3, 5.2, 5.3.6 or 5.4 if that is where it belongs.' (code: null). Reproduced twice.

title: 'Cleared to dispatch?' verdict and Validation tab omit blockers that stop packaging (STF 1789, application identity); counts differ between surfaces
root: Reproduced by API. GET /api/submissions/sequences/1/dispatch-readiness returned gate.blockers with exactly 4 entries: 7 error findings, 7 unapproved leaves, no Shadow Review, no Part 11 signature. It returned no STF and no identity blocker. In the same minute, assemble refused on FDA 1789 for the two m5.3.5.1 leaves. The Validation tab renders these dispatch-readiness findings (SubmissionCenter.tsx:26). The cause is that assessDispatchReadiness (server/services/ectd/assess-dispatch-readiness.ts:834-847) maps leaves into computeDispatchReadiness without studyId/stfFileTag. ReadinessLeaf (server/services/ectd/dispatch-readiness.ts:191-205) has no such fields, so the one coverage check auditStfCoverage (ectd4-validator.ts:157) is never run by the verdict. Only the packager runs it (regional-packager.ts:1056). Package identity is likewise never read by the assessment, yet freeze/dispatch refuse on it (submission-service.ts:1876 packageIdentityRefusal) and so does export (assemble-from-core.ts:582). Result: P-33's one dispatch verdict omits two refusals that every release step then makes. The other count differences (project 'Dossier readiness 0 of 72' = authored sections approved; Compile '3 of 36 required sections placed' = placement in the sequence; Compile Validate 41/43 = the compile route's own placement + identity findings, inflated per leaf when assembly is refused, see ectd-compile.ts:1224-1226) are different measures and not this defect.
fix: 1) Add optional studyId/stfFileTag to ReadinessLeaf. Pass l.studyId/l.stfFileTag from the leaf rows at assess-dispatch-readiness.ts:835. In computeDispatchReadiness, push auditStfCoverage(activeNonDelete…, {region, fileTagModelled:true}) findings, which are errors for US, warnings otherwise, so the Validation tab, the verdict and the packager share one check. 2) In assessDispatchReadiness, read readSubmissionPackageIdentity (already used by export) for the sequence's submission/region. When packageIdentityRefusal(...) returns one, add its message as a structural blocker or an error finding (code PACKAGE_IDENTITY_MISSING). The verdict then lists everything the package gate will refuse. Nothing new: both checks already exist and are only being composed into the existing gate.
test: In assess-dispatch-readiness.gates.test.ts (pglite): a US IND sequence with an m5.3.5.1 leaf missing studyId, on a program with no application number or D-U-N-S. Expect gate.blockers / findings to include an FDA 1789 (STF) error naming the leaf and a PACKAGE_IDENTITY_MISSING entry. Today neither appears.

Dispatch verdict: 'Four things stand between sequence 0000 and dispatch' (validation errors, unapproved docs, no shadow review, no Part 11 signature). Neither mentions (a) the FDA 1789 Study Tagging File rejection on the two m5.3.5.1 leaves (missing study id / file-tag), which is what makes assembly refuse, or (b) the missing package identity (no agency application number, no bound sponsor, no D-U-N-S, no regulatory contact). Compile & export Validate reports 41 findings including 4 PACKAGE_IDENTITY_MISSING errors. Compile reports 43 errors. Export returns 409 PACKAGE_IDENTITY_MISSING. title: Main demo project cannot reach a compiled package: every compile fails, and no project in the org has a successful one
root: Reproduced. GET /api/ectd-compile/6065271c-d4b0-4936-aad1-02855423a738/history returned two compilations, both status 'failed' with has_manifest false. No non-Sweep demo program checked had any compilation with a manifest. GET /sequences/1/leaves shows all 7 leaves with studyId null, stfFileTag null and sourceDocument.status 'undetermined'. The refusals are honest. The demo pack (scripts/demo/launch-demo/packs/biotech-content.mjs:73 and :117; leaf upsert in packs/biotech.mjs around :227) places Protocol and SAP at m5.3.5.1 with no study id or STF file-tag, which is FDA 1789 by design. It also records no application number, sponsor binding, D-U-N-S or regulatory contact, so package-identity refuses export and compile. Two secondary observations, not the blocker: (a) the 'undetermined' source label is by design for any non-text/plain vault byte source (server/services/ectd/submission-leaf-source-evidence.ts:223). It does not stop assembly, because the dry run reached the packager's STF check. (b) The compile's per-leaf 'unresolved-source'/hasContent false is a mislabel. isMaterialized is false for every leaf whenever assembleFailure != null (server/routes/ectd-compile.ts:1224-1226, used at :1051 and in leafPlacementFindings), so one identity refusal reads as N unresolved sources and inflates the error count to 43. That is worth an S5 follow-up. The demo sequence also carries a polluting leaf, 'Sweep RV 1.20 Introductory Statement C2C-101', at 1.20.

Approve the seven placed Vault versions so a compile can produce a manifest. Purge the 'Sweep RV 1.20' leaf from the demo sequence. title: Triage advances an agency letter's state in one click, with no confirmation, reason or undo
root: The behaviour is as described; I confirmed it by code reading and did not click it, to avoid changing the demo letter again. Triage is a deliberate, audited workflow step. PATCH /projects/:projectId/agency-communications/:eventId/advance (server/routes/c2c/communication-center.ts:938-1010) computes the transition server-side (pending_review→triaged/in_progress), refuses a re-apply with 409, and writes an audit entry with from/to status (logAuditEntry). It is not a release, signature or disposition event, so the Part 11 reason-for-change pattern does not apply. Whether official-correspondence closure needs a confirm/reason dialog is a product call for S10, not a defect in Triage.

title: Clicking the Filing card's 'Dispatch blocked' row shifts the whole app shell up 48px and hides the top bar
root: Reproduced in the running app at 1440x900. Before the click, document.scrollingElement scrollTop was 0 and scrollHeight 900. After clicking [data-testid=pj-status-market], scrollTop was 48, scrollHeight 949 and the header top was -48 (screenshot /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ClinicalSageAI-2-replit/0d57ee1e-feb7-587e-9df6-b4664672a1d4/scratchpad/sweep/verify-submission/v6-after-market-click.png). Open it on Submit (ProjectMarkets.tsx:580) is position:absolute (client/src/concept2cure/v2/styles/project-home-v2.css:553) with no positioned ancestor, so its offsetParent is BODY. It sits inside the scrolling .page-inner, which is position:static. After the stage change it lands at y≈948, outside the shell, and makes the document 49px taller than the viewport. openMarketOnSubmit (client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/ProjectHome.tsx:1705-1711) then calls scrollIntoView({block:'start'}). title: eCTD version is not recorded in compile history; v4.0 cannot be compiled; duplicate DTD line
root: Confirmed by API and code. History rows carry version '1.0' and no eCTD version. Both INSERTs hardcode it (server/routes/ectd-compile.ts:856 and :1318, `version` = '1.0'). The history table prints that constant under a 'Version' header (client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/EctdCompile.tsx:708-713), so it says nothing. The duplicated DTD line comes from CompilationHistoryTable rendering one PackageDtdValidation per history row (EctdCompile.tsx:724-725). It renders even for failed rows with has_manifest false. The visible heading is always 'Package DTD validation' (EctdCompileDtdEvidence.tsx:125) and the text 'DTD validation not recorded — unverified.', so two failed compiles print two identical blocks. v4.0 being reference-only is honestly labelled (EctdCompileReference.tsx:357-369). However, under RULE 3 an eCTD v4.0 RPS packager and validator already exist (server/services/ectd/ectd4/rps-packager.ts, rps-validator.ts; POST /api/ectd/v4/validate in server/routes/ectd-v4.ts) and the compile surface never reaches them. (2) Replace the meaningless 'Version' column with the eCTD format the compile assembled. The history SELECT can return it (all compiles today are v3.2.2, from assembled.bundle.format), or drop the column. (3) Separately, S5: reach the existing ectd4 rps-packager/rps-validator from the compile's v4.0 choice rather than leaving it reference-only.

title: Batch release always fails with HTTP 500: the client posts to /api/cmc/batch-records/NaN/release
root: Reproduced by API and in the UI. client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/cmcBatch.ts:109 maps `dbId: typeof row.id === 'number' ? row.id : Number(row.id)`, and the type at cmcBatch.ts:28 is `dbId?: number`. But cmc_batch_records.id is UUID (migrations/0006_regulatory_atoms.sql:65), so every row's dbId is NaN. Effects: (a) CmcModule.tsx:2565 posts to /api/cmc/batch-records/NaN/release. (b) CmcModule.tsx:2571 compares `x.dbId === target.dbId`, which is NaN===NaN, so a successful release would never update its row. (c) CmcModule.tsx:2610 uses `key={r.dbId ?? r.id}`, so every row has key NaN. I saw the React duplicate-key console error each time the Batch records tab rendered. Server side: server/api/cmc/batchRecordRoutes.ts:468-494 (POST /:id/release) and :288 (PUT /:id) never check the id. evaluateBatchForRelease (:404-415) runs `WHERE id = $1` on 'NaN', Postgres throws 22P02, and the route answers 500 with the raw message. I got `500 {"error":{"code":"22P02","message":"invalid input syntax for type uuid: \"NaN\""...}}`. client/src/lib/queryClient.ts INTERNAL_MARKERS (~:40-80) has no marker for 'invalid input syntax for type', so serverMessage passes the Postgres text into the toast. cmcSpec.ts already fixed this exact NaN-on-uuid bug for specifications (see the CmcSpecRow id comment), but the batch mapper was missed. The existing test client/src/concept2cure/v2/__tests__/cmcBatchMapping.test.ts:14-41 asserts numeric ids (55, '9'→9), so it pins the wrong contract. A note for the demo: with a real UUID, the server answers the seeded batch honestly. POST .../18aec524-.../release returned 409 RELEASE_EVIDENCE 'No QC result is recorded against batch C2C101-DP-2501 ... record them in QC testing first.' So once the id is fixed, a release also needs recorded QC results, which is a data matter.
fix: Do what cmcSpec.ts already does. In cmcBatch.ts, make `dbId?: string` and map `dbId: row.id == null ? undefined : String(row.id)`. CmcModule.tsx then needs only type adjustments: the URL, the row comparison at :2571 and the key at :2610 all work once the value is a string. In batchRecordRoutes.ts, add `if (!isUuid(id)) return res.status(400).json({ success:false, error:'This batch reference is not valid.' })` at the top of POST /:id/release and PUT /:id. isUuid already exists in server/middleware/uuidParam.ts and specificationRoutes.ts:726 uses it. Optionally add `/invalid input syntax for type/i` to INTERNAL_MARKERS in client/src/lib/queryClient.ts so no Postgres text reaches a toast. That file is outside S7/D5, so it falls under F1.
test: cmcBatchMapping.test.ts: batchRowFromApi({ id: '18aec524-5184-477b-969f-743ebe2c23ef', ... }).dbId === that uuid string (fails today: NaN). Route test: POST /api/cmc/batch-records/NaN/release with a valid body → 400, never 500, and no DB query issued.
observed: POST /api/cmc/batch-records/NaN/release returns 500 {"error":{"code":"22P02","message":"invalid input syntax for type uuid: \"NaN\""}}. The toast shows the raw database error: 'Couldn't release the batch — invalid input syntax for type uuid: "NaN".' The console also logs React 'Encountered two children with the same key ... NaN' each time the Batch records tab renders.

title: C2C-101 demo data has no drug substance, drug product or analytical methods, so none of its seeded specifications can be approved
root: This is the local database's seed state, not the code. The current seed packs write exactly what the tester found missing. scripts/demo/launch-demo/packs/work-areas.mjs ensureMaterials (:172-220) creates the substance and product, ensureMethods (:236-272) creates the method register, and packs/biotech.mjs:316 creates C2C-201. The database checked during the walk predated those commits (67e590b44, c900e79c6, 383a8097a). It has since been partly reseeded with the current seeder. At 18:50 UTC, after the tester's walk, GET /api/cmc/drug-substances, drug-products and analytical-methods for C2C-101 returned 'C2C-101' (id 4), 'C2C-101 injection' (id 4) and AM-101..AM-105. '[Demo · Biotech] C2C-201 oral JAK1 inhibitor' now exists too. One part remains: all five methods are in status 'validation', not 'validated'. ensureMethods signs the ICH Q2 validation only when the seed run is given a signer credential, and this run was not. So specification approval is still refused, now because each method is unvalidated. That refusal is an honest, specific 409 and correct behaviour.
fix: No code change. Before the demo, re-run the launch-demo seed against the demo database with the signer credential the pack accepts. That signs AM-101..AM-105 to 'validated', and specification approval then succeeds on C2C-101. Then confirm with GET /api/cmc/analytical-methods?projectId=6065271c-... that every AM-10x reads status 'validated'.
test: Demo rehearsal check: after seeding, every seeded C2C-101 specification's named method resolves to a validated row in the register, so Approve does not return METHOD_NOT_IN_REGISTER or METHOD_NOT_VALIDATED.
observed: Before I added anything, Substance & product showed 'No drug substances yet', 'No drug products yet' and the method library at '0/0 validated'. Yet specifications, batches and stability studies all name 'C2C-101 drug substance' and 'C2C-101 drug product'. GET /api/cmc/analytical-methods?projectId=<C2C-101> held none of the seeded AM-101..AM-105. title: Contradiction sweep raises false High 'specification_conflict' findings and tasks by comparing unrelated attributes' limits
root: Confirmed. GET /api/cmc/module3-os/contradictions/<C2C-101> holds two High specification_conflict findings, keyed 'shelf' and 'release', each listing potency vs SEC purity vs HCP vs appearance/pH vs particles. server/services/cmc-impact-contradiction-engine.ts:57-77 groups by the KEYS of spec.acceptanceCriteria and flags any key that carries more than one distinct value. The register's real shape differs. One quality_specifications row is one attribute: material_name is the attribute and material_type is DS or DP (client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/cmcSpec.ts:14-21), and acceptance_criteria is always {release, shelf}. server/services/cmc/contradiction-registers.ts:85 passes `material_name as materialName, acceptance_criteria as acceptanceCriteria` straight through. So every pair of specs with different limits 'conflicts' under 'release' and 'shelf'. The same reader feeds the final export gate (server/services/cmc/final-export-gate.ts:213), so the false findings also reach that gate. Specification conflicts are severity 'high', not 'critical', so this fault cannot block export by itself. The sweep running on a biologic is not itself wrong: it reads records and composes nothing, so P-28 does not apply to it.
fix: Converge the register reader onto the engine's contract, without touching the engine, which sits outside S7. In contradiction-registers.ts, select material_type as well. Reshape each row to `{ materialName: material_type, acceptanceCriteria: { [`${material_type} · ${material_name} (release)`]: release, [`${material_type} · ${material_name} (shelf)`]: shelf } }`, skipping empty limits. A conflict then requires the same material, the same attribute and the same limit kind with different values, which is the real case: two recorded specs for one attribute that disagree.
test: Unit test: detectContradictions(readContradictionRegisters(fake pool returning five rows of distinct attributes, each with {release, shelf})) yields no specification_conflict (fails today: two). The same test with two rows for 'Drug substance · potency' and different release limits yields exactly one.
observed: Toast: 'Contradiction sweep complete — 3 findings recorded. 2 raised as tasks, 1 already open.' The history lists, at High severity, 'Conflicting acceptance criteria for "shelf": C2C-101 drug substance — potency="70–130% of reference standard" vs ... purity by SEC-HPLC="Monomer ≥ 95.0% ..." vs ... host cell protein="≤ 100 ppm" vs ... appearance and pH ... vs ... subvisible particles ...', and the same for "release". These are different attributes, not conflicting limits. The sweep also runs on this biologic project even though Module 3 compile is refused for it.

title: Composed §3.1 says the drug substance is the drug product ('The drug substance is Sweep SM-70411 tablets')
root: Confirmed by code reading. I did not re-run the compile, to avoid writing to another tester's project. server/services/module3Composer.ts:3125-3126 composes §3.1 with `val(m, 'name')`. val (:233-239) returns the first source whose payload has the field. §3.1's rule (:217) admits both drug_substance and drug_product sources. The drug_product payload also carries `name: productName` (server/services/cmc-write-through.ts:305). Sources load newest first (server/services/cmc/module3-compile.ts:49 `ORDER BY updated_at DESC`), so once the product is recorded or updated after the substance, §3.1 says 'The drug substance is <product name>'. §3.3 at :3161 has the same bug. §3.2.S.1 is correct because only drug_substance sources reach it. This is the 'order sources arrived in' failure that the file's own comment at :3163-3167 already fixed for reference standards.
fix: In the '3.1' and '3.3' generators, read each field from its recorded type, as §3.3 already does for reference standards. Use `const name = val(m.filter((s) => s.sourceType === 'drug_substance'), 'name');` and `const form = val(m.filter((s) => s.sourceType === 'drug_product'), 'dosageFormDescription');`. module3Composer.ts matches no open package except the F1 catch-all.

Same assertion for §3.3.

title: Variation assessment for a biologic cites 21 CFR 314.70 (NDA/ANDA) instead of 21 CFR 601.12
root: Confirmed by code reading. server/services/cmc/supac-classifier.ts classifyFda (:194-262) pushes '21 CFR 314.70 — Supplements and other changes to an approved application' unconditionally (:200). It returns PAS 'per 21 CFR 314.70(b)' (:207) for every dosageFormFamily, including 'biologic' (declared at :42). No 21 CFR 601.12 branch exists, and the only biologic-specific handling is the BE short-circuit at :355. So a BLA change cites the NDA/ANDA regulation. CmcModule.tsx:2901-2906 renders CmcVariationAssessment when `launchScopeEnforced === false`, and otherwise shows 'Postapproval variation assessment is outside this release'. title: Stability trend on the seeded demo study refuses every series: it reads the study-type code 'LT' as a second storage condition
root: Reproduced. POST /api/cmc/stability-studies/1/trending returns series with condition '5°C ± 3°C + LT' and reason CONDITION_NOT_SEPARABLE. This is not only seed data. The product's own Register study form writes the same shape: client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/cmcRegisterForms.ts:400-414 splits 'LT|5°C ± 3°C' and stores `storageConditions: [storageCode, condition]`. The UI-registered study 5 ('Sweep DS long-term 5C') reads ['LT','25°C ± 2°C / 60% ± 5% RH']. The server treats that array as a set of storage conditions. server/services/cmc/recorded-stability.ts:350-356 conditionKey joins every entry with ' + ', and :468 (poolability) and :1033 (trending) read any ' + ' as multi-condition and refuse. The study-type code (LT/INT/ACC/STR/REF, the client's STAB_STORAGE_LABEL at CmcModule.tsx:1527) is counted as a second condition. So every study registered through the UI is refused for trend and poolability. The seed (packs/biotech-work-content.mjs:111/223/234) copies the UI's shape. After the fix, the seeded study would still be refused honestly with INSUFFICIENT_POINTS (3 points, 5 needed), which is correct for the data.
fix: Converge the server reader onto the client's stored contract, so stored rows need no migration. In conditionKey (recorded-stability.ts:350), drop entries that are bare study-type codes: `.filter(c => !/^(LT|INT|ACC|STR|REF)$/i.test(c))`. Do the same anywhere the conditions are matched against result rows' recorded condition (the declaredCondition path near :330-345). One study at [code, condition] then has one condition, and trend and poolability proceed or refuse on the data alone.
test: assessRecordedTrending({ storageConditions: ['LT','5°C ± 3°C'], stabilityData: five numeric pulls of one parameter }) returns ok with one series at condition '5°C ± 3°C', not CONDITION_NOT_SEPARABLE (fails today). conditionKey(['LT','5°C ± 3°C']) === '5°C ± 3°C'.
observed: Toast: 'No series on this study could be assessed — see the reason against each of the 3 below.' Each series says: 'the study is placed at more than one storage condition (5°C ± 3°C + LT) and these results record none ...'. The study is at one condition (Long-term, 5°C ± 3°C).

title: Stability register table overflows its card at 1440px; the Shelf life and History actions are off-screen
root: Reproduced at 1440x900. The stability register table measured 1229px wide inside a 1006px parent with overflow-x 'visible'. Its right edge sat at x=1578 against a 1440px viewport. Document scrollWidth stayed 1440, so the overflow is clipped, which leaves the right-hand actions out of reach. In CmcModule.tsx:2064/2076, the `<table className="reg-tbl">` with 11 columns plus StabilityRowActions sits directly in `.pj-card-b` (padding 0). The only rule that makes a reg-tbl scroll inside its card is client/src/concept2cure/v2/styles/app-v2.css:417-420, and it sits inside `@media (max-width: 640px)`, so at laptop widths a wide register table has no containment.
fix: Move the containment rule out of the phone-only media query, so a wide table scrolls inside its card at every width: `.c2c-v2 :is(.pj-card, .pj-card-b, .reg-card) > .reg-tbl { display:block; overflow-x:auto; }` (D0 owns app-v2.css; D5 covers styles/** too). Alternatively, in CmcModule.tsx only, wrap this one table in `<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>`. Either keeps Shelf life and History reachable.

title: Wrong-password e-signature shows a generic 'HTTP 401..' message
root: Confirmed by code reading. The section-approval handler at client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/CmcModule.tsx:860-878 special-cases only 409. A 401 {error:'REAUTH_PASSWORD_INVALID'} falls to :877: `'Couldn’t approve section ' + key + ' — ' + specErr(json, status) + '. Nothing was persisted.'` specErr (:1223-1230) returns serverMessage(json), which correctly rejects the enum token. Its fallback 'The server did not accept the change (HTTP 401).' already ends in a period, hence the '..'. The sibling signing flows in the same file already handle this: specification approval at :1386 ('Approval not signed — re-authentication failed...') and batch release at :2568.
fix: Add the same 401 branch the sibling flows use before the generic !res.ok toast at :876: `if (res.status === 401) { fireToast('Section ' + target.key + ' not signed — your password was not accepted. Nothing was approved.', 'error'); return; }`. Also stop doubling the period, e.g. strip a trailing '.' from specErr's result before appending '. Nothing was persisted.'

title: Module 3 build board lists 'Draft in editor' but has no way to open the composed section, and its summary goes stale after compile
root: Confirmed by code reading. The build board's section rows (CmcModule3Build.tsx ~:680-705) offer only Build, History and Evidence. The build state does carry each section's `artifactId` (CmcModule3Build.tsx:62), and BUILD_STATE_META labels the state 'draft in editor' (:177), yet nothing reads artifactId to open it. The summary is not stale data. run() calls bump() and reloads build-state after compile (:291-292). The label is wrong. server/api/cmc/module3BuildStateRoutes.ts:135 counts `buildableSections` as 'has sources and is not approved'. BuildCounts (CmcModule3Build.tsx:107) prints that count as 'ready to compile', so compiled, unapproved sections keep counting as 'ready to compile'.

Or count client-side only sections whose buildState === 'extraction_complete' for 'ready to compile'. 2) For a row with `s.artifactId`, add an 'Open' action through the existing editor handoff: setEditorTarget({ docType:null, docId:s.artifactId, programId, code:'3.2…' }) then nav('document-authoring'), as openSavedAuthoring does in client/src/concept2cure/v2/authoringHandoff.ts:197-202. title: Biologic project: actions that will always be refused stay enabled, and the Overview empty state suggests sections will appear
root: Confirmed by code reading. The refusals themselves are correct: P-28, honest 409s in the server's words, and the build board already renders an out-of-scope EmptyState when build-state answers 409 (CmcModule3Build.tsx:428-447). But the header actions ignore that answer. 'Compile Module 3' and 'Run contradiction sweep' are `disabled={Boolean(busy)}` only (CmcModule3Build.tsx:416-420). The sweep is legitimate on a biologic; Compile is not. The Overview's empty state (CmcModule.tsx:1091) always promises 'They appear here with their approval state once created', even for a product the boundary refuses. CmcQuality.tsx (~:280-300) shows the same pattern for the QbD actions. This is a UX defect, not a boundary error.
fix: Reuse the 409 the surface already holds. In CmcModule3Build.tsx, `disabled={Boolean(busy) || build.status === 409}` on Compile, with `title={build.error}`. Leave the sweep enabled. In CmcQuality.tsx, disable the ICH check, control strategy, Q1E and poolability actions when its read returned 409, showing the server's reason. In CmcModule.tsx:1091, when the build-state read is 409, render the server's boundary sentence instead of 'They appear here ... once created'. Nothing new: the 409 code and words already reach the client.

title: Forms and registers show raw enum values, bad grammar and small-molecule defaults on a biologic
root: Confirmed by code reading. client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/cmcRegisterForms.ts passes raw token arrays as select and seg options: PROCESS_SIDES (:2003), PROCESS_VALIDATION_STATUSES (:2006), CHARACTERIZATION_SCOPES (:2107), CHARACTERIZATION_STATUSES (:2109), PV_STATUSES (:586) and COMPARABILITY_STATUSES (:896). title: Main demo project page is cluttered with test work projects and test Vault documents; Module 3 section counts disagree
root: Not reproduced as a code defect. Partly classified from code reading because of the time-box. title: Biostatistics 'Open in editor' and 'Save as a working document' always fail with 503 PROJECT_ACCESS_UNAVAILABLE, so no engine document reaches the editor
root: Reproduced in the UI. I opened Biostatistics for C2C-101 and clicked 'Open in editor'. POST /api/ana-biostats/document (save_to_authoring) returned 503 {"error":"PROJECT_ACCESS_UNAVAILABLE","message":"Current project access could not be verified. Nothing was changed."} and the page showed 'Could not confirm whether the document was saved...'. Cause: the access token carries organizationId as the STRING "2" (decoded JWT from dev-login: "organizationId":"2"; server/middleware/auth.ts:54 types it `organizationId?: string`, and :260 copies it onto req.user). server/routes/ana-biostats.ts:41-48 resolveOrganizationId returns that value unconverted, despite its `number` type. :265 then passes it to saveStatisticalWorkbenchDocument (:221-235) as tenantId. From there it goes to server/services/ana-biostats/statistical-document-save.ts:61 authorizeAuthoringProgram, then server/services/authoring/authoring-program-access.ts canAccessReportProject(tenantId, ...). There server/services/report-os/project-access.ts:9-12 positiveId rejects any non-number and throws 'Invalid project access identity'. The catch in authorizeAuthoringProgram turns that into the 503. The earlier SQL steps pass because Postgres coerces '2'. The route test server/routes/__tests__/ana-biostats-save-on-request-client.test.ts:25 uses a numeric organizationId: 1, which is why it never caught this. The sibling resolver in server/routes/ana-biostats-governed-documents.ts:69-77 already does Number() plus a positive-integer check. The workbench's 'Insert into document' goes through /api/authoring/docs and succeeds, which confirms the fault is local to this resolver. Secondary: client/src/concept2cure/v2/authoringHandoff.ts:117 maps every 5xx to 'unknown', so the UI says 'could not confirm whether saved' while the server says definitively that nothing changed. That conservative mapping is deliberate, because a 5xx can follow a committed write. This particular refusal, though, is raised before any write.
fix: In server/routes/ana-biostats.ts resolveOrganizationId, coerce the claim the way ana-biostats-governed-documents.ts:69-77 already does: `const n = Number(raw); if (!Number.isSafeInteger(n) || n < 1) throw new OrganizationContextRequired(); return n;`. Apply the same coercion to the identical resolvers in biostat-design-stats.ts:101 and biostatPlatform.ts:79. Optionally, in authoringHandoff.ts writeHandoffStage, treat a 503 whose body code is PROJECT_ACCESS_UNAVAILABLE (raised before any write, 'Nothing was changed') as 'refused', so the notice says nothing was saved.
test: In ana-biostats-save-on-request-client.test.ts, set req.user.organizationId to the string '1', as real tokens carry it. Assert that the save reaches authorizeAuthoringProgram/canAccessReportProject with the number 1 and answers 201, not 503. This test is red today.
observed: POST /api/ana-biostats/document with action 'save_to_authoring' returns 503 {"success":false,"error":"PROJECT_ACCESS_UNAVAILABLE","message":"Current project access could not be verified. Nothing was changed."}. The page stays on Biostatistics and shows: 'Could not confirm whether the document was saved. Check working documents in the original project before creating another copy; the document is still here.' The dev log has the cause at every attempt: {"programId":"6065271c-...","tenantId":"2","forWrite":true,"message":"Invalid project access identity"}, msg 'Authoring project access could not be verified'. Note that tenantId is the string "2", not a number. The UI's 'could not confirm whether it was saved' also contradicts the server's definite 'Nothing was changed'.

title: Three built-in worked-example presets fail to size: Non-inferiority, Diagnostic accuracy, ROC / AUC
root: Reproduced by POST /api/ana-biostats/compute with the exact preset inputs from Biostatistics.tsx:359-362. ni: validation error 'Effect size must be positive'. ivd: 422 'Diagnostic-accuracy sizing needs ... (nonInferiorityMargin)'. roc: 'Effect size must be positive' plus 'At least sensitivity or specificity target is required'. The engine itself sizes both designs: NI with effect 0.0001 returns 312, and AUC with a positive effect returns 24 via Hanley & McNeil. The validator blocks them. server/services/ana-biostats/input-normalizer.ts:159-161 rejects effectSize <= 0 for every design. That includes non-inferiority, where a zero true difference is the standard assumption (computation-engine.ts:328-330 uses |delta - margin|), and auc_roc, which is sized from aucTarget/aucNull (computation-engine.ts:145, 1143-1156). input-normalizer.ts:299-303 demands sensitivity or specificity for studyType diagnostic_accuracy even when endpointType is auc_roc. The Diagnostic accuracy preset (client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/Biostatistics.tsx:360) omits nonInferiorityMargin, which computeDiagnostic requires by its no-assumption contract. The run-together ROC message comes from Biostatistics.tsx:639-643, which joins the messages with ' ' when they have no terminal punctuation.
fix: In input-normalizer.ts, accept effectSize === 0 for non_inferiority and equivalence. Skip the effect-size check, and the sensitivity/specificity requirement at :300, when endpointType === 'auc_roc'. In Biostatistics.tsx:360, give the ivd preset a stated nonInferiorityMargin (for example 0.05) so the performance goal is explicit, not assumed. At :643, join the validation messages with '. ' or render them as a list.
test: A test that runs every BS_PRESETS input through anaBiostatsOrchestrator.quickCompute and expects validation.valid with a computation present. It fails today for ni, ivd and roc.
observed: Non-inferiority (fills Effect (d)=0, NI margin=-0.4): 'The statistical engine did not size this design — Effect size must be positive'. Diagnostic accuracy: HTTP 422 POST /api/ana-biostats/compute 'Diagnostic-accuracy sizing needs the margin below the expected sensitivity/specificity that defines the performance goal (nonInferiorityMargin); none was given, and none is assumed.' ROC / AUC (Expected AUC 0.85, Null AUC 0.5): 'Effect size must be positive At least sensitivity or specificity target is required for diagnostic accuracy studies' (two messages run together with no separator). In each case: 'No document — the design was not sized'.

title: The sample size document reports 'Effect size 0.47' after the treatment rate changes; the 'Delta rate' input never re-derives
root: Reproduced by API. I took the C2C-101-201 design's adapter input (effectSize 0.47, controlRate 0.08, treatmentRate 0.55) and set treatmentRate to 0.30. Compute sized on effect 0.22 (77 per group, two-proportion z-test, p2=0.300). The Sample Size Rationale still printed '| Effect size | 0.47 | Stated |', 'Base case 252 ... Effect size = 0.4700' and 'Effect size: current 0.47, breakpoint 0.4465'. Cause: server/services/ana-biostats/input-normalizer.ts:186 keeps the stated effectSize (`raw.effectSize ?? derive`) even when both rates are supplied. Meanwhile computation-engine.ts:336-340 binaryRates uses treatmentRate for p2. Everything downstream reads input.effectSize: the assumptions table, the scenario deltas (computation-engine.ts:1424), the sensitivity breakpoints (judgment-engine.ts:566-581) and document-generator.ts:623 ('to detect an effect size of ${input.effectSize}'). In the client, Biostatistics.tsx:1035 'Delta rate' is an independent input that the rate inputs at :1039-1040 never update.
fix: In input-normalizer normalize, for a binary endpoint with both rates, set normalized effectSize = treatmentRate - controlRate. Add a warning when a stated effectSize differs, so the computation, judgment and documents all read the delta that was actually sized. In Biostatistics.tsx, when controlRate or treatmentRate changes on a binary design, set effectSize to their difference, or show Delta rate read-only.
test: Call documentGenerator.generate('sample_size_rationale', ...) after quickCompute on {endpointType:'binary', controlRate:0.08, treatmentRate:0.30, effectSize:0.47}. The content must state 0.22 and must not contain '0.47'.
observed: The sizing uses p1=0.08, p2=0.300 (162 subjects at power 0.8, or 168 at power 0.9). The Delta rate input still shows 0.47. The document's assumptions table says 'Effect size | 0.47 | Stated | High', the scenario table says 'Base case 168 ... Effect size = 0.4700', and the sensitivity line says 'Effect size: current 0.47, breakpoint 0.4465'. The real difference is 0.22. Confirmed by a direct POST /api/ana-biostats/document with treatmentRate 0.30 and effectSize 0.47.

title: Protocol DOCX export contains raw Markdown as literal text; the PDF leaves inline Markdown and pipe tables unrendered
root: Confirmed by reading the code; I did not re-run the export in the time box. The repository already documents the defect in server/services/agency-responses/response-package-docx.ts:5-8. ProtocolDevWorkspace.tsx:198-216 posts the assembled Markdown from GET /api/protocol-export/:id to the chat-artifact exporters. server/services/docxGenerator.ts:30-47 generateDocxBuffer splits on blank lines and writes each block as a single plain TextRun, so there are no headings, bold, lists or tables and every Markdown mark prints literally. root: Confirmed by code reading. client/src/concept2cure/v2/engineResultHtml.ts:53-58 engineResultCellText renders object cells with JSON.stringify, which produces the raw per-look array, and numbers with String(value) by explicit choice ('No rounding'). title: Alpha 0.025 is sized as two-sided, which likely over-sizes the C2C-101 design
root: The engine respects what the design records. The demo protocol states 'a two-sided alpha of 0.025 per comparison' (scripts/demo/launch-demo/packs/biotech-content.mjs:102, 267, 320; design alpha 0.025 at biotech-work-content.mjs:334). So 'α=0.025 (two-sided)' is a faithful reading of the record. The 'Two-sided 0.05 unless justified' line is generic guidance, and per-comparison multiplicity is the justification.

One-sided 0.025 (z=1.96) gives 19 per group, about 63 in total. The same document's 'Regulatory Considerations' say 'Two-sided significance level of 0.05 unless justified'.

title: Wording and data inconsistencies in engine and protocol text
root: Several small real defects. (a) Randomization: server/services/ana-biostats/document-generator.ts:909 prints `${input.allocationRatio}:1 across ${groups} arms`, which gives '1:1 across 3 arms'; reproduced by API. (b) The gap list checks only the header synopsis field: server/services/authoring/workflow-source-import.ts:117 `if (!document.synopsis?.trim())`, ignoring a saved Synopsis section in sourceRows.sections. (f) The section-order warning on a fresh working copy comes from client/src/concept2cure/v2/editor/DocumentWorkbench.tsx:4651. I did not trace why the import writes sections out of code order.

(c) Pluralise the counts. (d) Drop the toLowerCase and use the label as written. (e) Map enums through the existing label vocabularies (STUDY_TYPE_LABELS, ENDPOINT_TYPE_LABELS and similar, already used by Biostatistics VocabSelect). (f) Write imported sections in section-code order.

root: Reproduced by API: POST /api/mdx/rbm-kris for C2C-101 with no currentValue returned 500 INTERNAL_ERROR 'Something went wrong while create-kri...', correlation 979d4e6f-7adc-4993-9775-89926cdecf24. The INSERT at server/routes/mdx-rbm.ts:505-511 uses $11 twice. It is the bare current_value, where the column coerces it to numeric, and it is also inside `CASE WHEN $11 IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE NOW() END` (line 507). A NullTest never coerces its argument, so that Param node keeps the unknown type while the parameter's global type resolves to numeric. Postgres' parameter-resolution check then raises 42P08 'could not determine data type of parameter $11'. It fails whether or not currentValue is sent, so the route can never succeed. The same statement is copied in the AnA tool path, server/services/rbm/rbm-actuator.ts:183, so AnA's KRI create is broken too. The 'create-kri' wording comes from server/lib/api-response.ts:195, which puts the internal `where` handler label into the user-facing message on every route.
fix: Type the parameter in both copies: `CASE WHEN $11::numeric IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE NOW() END`. Equivalently, cast the value as `$11::numeric` in both places. Files: mdx-rbm.ts:507 and rbm-actuator.ts:183. A separate, optional F1 change: keep `where` in the log only, and give users a plain sentence such as 'The change could not be saved. The problem has been logged.' That change touches 5 tests that assert the current wording, so keep it out of the RBM fix.
test: Add a PGlite route test in the style of server/routes/__tests__/rbm-approval-signature.pglite.test.ts. It POSTs /rbm-kris with no currentValue and asserts 201 with status 'not_evaluated' and evaluated_at null. It then POSTs with currentValue 0.9 and asserts 201 with evaluated_at set. Add the same check for rbm-actuator's create-KRI path. Both fail today with 42P08.
