title: A new study cannot start its risk assessment without AnA: seed buttons never appear
root: Confirmed from the code chain, and the live C2C-101 board shows the same attention item. buildAttentionFeed (server/services/rbm/risk-report.ts:260-266) always adds 'No source feeds are tracked for this study' when no feed exists, which is every new study. rbmBoardHasData (client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/rbmBoard.ts:282-295) counts `board.attention.length > 0` as data, so it is always true for a selected study. KRIs (line 514) and QTLs (line 621) have deterministic seed buttons; the assessment does not. Without a model, the only remaining route is the AnA turn, which returns 503.

root: Reproduced at 1440x900 with the AnA dock open (352px): the '.rbm-ract-cols .rbm-card.grow' register card spans 666-1004px with clientWidth 336 and overflow-x hidden, while its table's scrollWidth is 815. title: The RACT author is offered 'Approve assessment' but can never approve, which blocks plan generation for the demo user
root: Partly correct behaviour, partly a defect. The refusal itself is right: the two-person rule (21 CFR Part 11 §11.10(d)) at server/routes/mdx-rbm.ts:1131-1140 is deliberate, and 'Generate from RACT' correctly needs an approved RACT. RACT id 2 for C2C-101 has created_by 1 (jm.smith) and created_at 2026-11-09T18:35:03, so a tester seeded it today. That is local data, not the shipped demo seed. The defect is the order and what the UI shows. The route verifies password and MFA first (reverifySigner, line 1100), and only afterwards reads created_by and refuses self-approval (lines 1116-1140). So an author is put through the whole signing ceremony, and their failed attempts count toward lockout, before learning they can never sign. P-27 moved the signing-authority check ahead of the password for exactly this reason (comment at lines 1094-1096), but the authorship check was left after it. The board's assessment object (server/routes/mdx-rbm-board.ts:546-570) does not expose created_by or an 'authored by you' flag. The UI therefore offers 'Approve assessment' to the author (RbmSurfacesA.tsx:377) and opens GovernedApprovalDialog (lines 437-448) with no warning.
fix: Server: read the row's created_by and status before reverifySigner, using a plain SELECT. Return the 403 RBM_SELF_APPROVAL (and the 409 for a non-draft) without asking for the password. Keep the existing FOR UPDATE re-check inside the transaction. Board: add `authoredByViewer: rbmRecordedAuthor(a.createdBy) === userId`, or createdBy, to the assessment object and its RbmBoard type. UI: when authoredByViewer is true, replace the Approve button with the note 'You wrote this assessment; a second person must approve it', using the existing copy. For the demo, have a second account sign, or seed the C2C-101 RACT under another author; that is a DATA-package decision.
test: In rbm-approval-signature.pglite.test.ts: the author POSTs /rbm-assessments/:id/approve with a WRONG password. Assert 403 RBM_SELF_APPROVAL, and assert that the password verifier was not called and no failed-attempt row was written. Today it returns the password failure first. Add a client test that RbmRact shows no 'Approve assessment' button when board.assessment.authoredByViewer is true.
observed: Neither the dialog nor the page says the signer wrote this assessment. The server refuses self-approval only after it has checked the password (mdx-rbm.ts:1100 reverifySigner, then 1131-1140 returns 403 'You wrote this risk assessment, so you cannot also approve it...'), and the UI offers no way to send the RACT to a second approver. So the demo user cannot activate the RACT, and 'Generate from RACT' stays refused: 409 'This study's risk assessment has not been approved...'. The monitoring plan, plan actions, site-visit scheduling and 'Escalate to action' are all unreachable. I did not submit the signature: there is no password for the dev sign-in, and failed signatures count toward lockout of the shared account.

title: Risk review report says 'Ok' and 'approval pending' for a study that has no risk assessment
root: Reproduced on the live C2C-101 board report: 'ok | Site risk & oversight | 0 sites scored' and 'ok | Patient profiles | 0 subjects profiled'. In buildRiskReview (server/services/rbm/risk-report.ts), several sections pass on empty data. The RACT section (line 70) is 'ok' when total is 0, because only high or open counts raise it, and this happens even when there is no assessment at all. KRIs (line 84) are 'ok' when total is 0. Site risk (line 119) is 'ok' when 0 sites are scored. Patient profiles (line 126) are 'ok' when 0 subjects are profiled. Line 182 defaults framework to 'ich_e6r3' when there is no assessment. The client header (RbmSurfacesA.tsx:208-210) prints R.framework raw and says 'assessment approval pending' whenever approved is false, including when no assessment exists. The file's own rule (lines 79-80: 'an unevaluated indicator is an oversight gap... never rolled up as though it were green') is not applied to empty sections.

Cases: no assessment ('No risk assessment recorded'), 0 KRIs, 0 sites scored ('Site risk has not been scored'), 0 subjects profiled ('Patient profiles have not been scored'). Count them in attentionCount. Return `framework: input.assessment?.framework ?? null`, and a `hasAssessment` flag or approved:null. In RbmReport, show 'No risk assessment yet' instead of 'assessment approval pending' when there is none.

Risk assessment (RACT / Critical-to-Quality) | Ok | 0 CtQ factors (0 critical, 0 open). | No open critical factors. | Key Risk Indicators | Ok | 0 KRIs tracked'. title: KRI readings accept impossible values; the demo board shows 'Dropout rate 9 ratio' as its top red KRI
root: The value on the demo board is local pollution. C2C-101's 'Dropout rate' (KRI id 15) carries one reading of 9.0000, rbm_kri_values id 50, observed 2026-11-09T18:38:49 today. Another tester's walk entered it; it is not demo seed data. That one reading drives 'KRI red: Dropout rate' in the attention feed and in the report. The server does accept any number: appendKriValueBody is `value: z.number()` at server/routes/mdx-rbm.ts:591, and so do createKriBody and patchKriBody. But the data model has no per-KRI range, and the unit is free text. A rule keyed on unit 'ratio' would be wrong: the seeded 'Enrollment vs target' KRI (server/services/rbm/rbm-engine.ts:285) is also a 'ratio' and legitimately exceeds 1 when a study over-enrols. Range validation therefore needs a bound per KRI, which nothing records today, and adding that field is a RULE 6 or founder decision, not a repair.
fix: Before the demo, correct the C2C-101 'Dropout rate' reading, or soft-delete reading 50 and reset KRI 15 to not_evaluated, and also clean the tester-entered 'CRF entry lag' readings. If range checks are wanted later, carry an optional min/max on the DEFAULT_KRIS entries, stored in the existing rbm_kris metadata column if it fits. Then refuse a reading outside the range with a 422 that names the range. That needs a founder decision under RULE 6.
test: Only if a founder approves bounds: a route test that POST /rbm-kris/:id/values with value 9 on a KRI whose metadata bounds are 0 to 1 returns 422 and writes no row.
observed: The server accepts 9 (POST /api/mdx/rbm-kris/23/values {"value":9}) and the KRI turns Red. title: Duplicate CAPA numbers in the organisation's CAPA register
root: Reproduced from GET /api/capa-mdr/capa. There are two CAPA-2026-0001 rows, but they belong to different projects: the Sweep CAPA in program 796c69b8 and the Lumen CAPA in program 980ee422. Numbering per project is a deliberate design. nextCode (server/services/capa-mdr/capaMdr.service.ts:137-169) takes the maximum sequence 'FOR THIS PROGRAM AND YEAR', and migrations/20260919_capa_code_uniqueness_per_program.sql changed the unique index to (program_id, code) on purpose. The Quality CAPA register (client/src/concept2cure/quality/qmsCapaRegister.tsx:84-88) lists the whole organisation's CAPAs, ignoring the open project, and has no project column. So a number that is unique only within a project appears twice in one org-wide list. Whether CAPA numbers must be unique across the organisation, which is the usual QMS convention for audits, is a product decision: it reverses a deliberate migration.
fix: Option A, org-unique numbers: nextCode reads the maximum by organization_id and year instead of program_id. Amend the creating migration's index to (organization_id, code) in place, under RULE 1, with a dated note, and add conditional conversion in the 20260919 file. Existing duplicates would need renumbering. Option B, keep per-project numbers: add a Project column to the register, or prefix the displayed code with the project code, so a number identifies one CAPA in the org-wide list. Either option needs the founder to rule.
test: Under option A: two createCapaRecord calls in different programs of the same org, in the same year, must return different capaCodes. Under option B: a QmsRecords register test asserts that each row shows its project label.

title: Quality surface hits its own document rate limit during normal use
root: Confirmed by code reading only; I did not reproduce it, and the shared tester load is a real contributor. GET /api/mdx/qms/documents and /documents/review-due contain the path segment 'documents', so getCategory (server/middleware/redisRateLimiter.ts:433) puts them in the 'documents' bucket. That bucket allows 20 requests a minute per user (server/config/platform-limits.ts:145-149) and is meant for downloads, exports and writes. DOCUMENT_METADATA_READS (redisRateLimiter.ts:400-406) already moved list and metadata reads of this same kind to 'document_metadata' (600 a minute per identity), after the 2026-10-08 and 2026-10-25 QA incidents described at lines 380-398. The QMS register's list, review-due and per-document training reads (quality/hooks.ts:27, 45 and 203) were never added. Two testers share user 1 and the dev build double-mounts, so 20 a minute is easy to exceed. The register keeps its earlier data, so the user saw no error.
fix: Add the QMS register's GET metadata reads to DOCUMENT_METADATA_READS: `/(^|\/)mdx\/qms\/documents\/?$/`, `/(^|\/)mdx\/qms\/documents\/review-due\/?$/` and `/(^|\/)mdx\/qms\/documents\/[^/]+\/training-assignments\/?$/`. Controlled-copy downloads, the editor read and writes stay in 'documents'.

title: An AnA conversation whose turn fails is not saved or listed, although the UI says turns are preserved
root: Reproduced by API. POST /api/ana-ri/stream returned 503 GATEWAY_UNAVAILABLE, and GET /api/chat/threads stayed {"threads":[]}. The server refuses at server/routes/ana-ri/stream.ts:1036-1040, before getOrCreateThread (:1410) and saveMessage (:1427). Refusing before persisting is consistent with the other refusals. The defect is the UI's claim. streamRefusalText (client/src/concept2cure/components/ana/useAnaChat.ts:666-668) says 'Prior turns are preserved', which on a first turn suggests this one was kept, and it never says this message was not saved. title: The AI circuit breaker takes down every /api/ana-ri read, not just model calls
root: Reproduced. One POST /api/ana-ri/stream (503 GATEWAY_UNAVAILABLE) was followed by two GET /api/ana-ri/agent-activity calls, both 503 {status:'circuit_open'}; before the turn the same GET returned 200. server/bootstrap/register-ai-routes.ts:35 mounts aiCircuitBreaker over the whole /api/ana-ri router, reads included. The middleware (server/middleware/circuitBreaker.ts:323-349) records every 5xx, including the deliberate configuration refusal GATEWAY_UNAVAILABLE, and never records a success. close() is reachable only through execute()/allowSingleRequest(), which the middleware does not call, so `failures` (:180-192) only grows. After 10 cumulative 5xx since boot, every later 5xx re-opens the shared, process-wide breaker for 30 s (startup/routes.ts:71-77) for every user.
fix: (1) In register-ai-routes.ts, apply aiCircuitBreaker only to model-calling requests: wrap it so GET requests skip it, or mount it on the stream router only. (2) In createCircuitBreakerMiddleware's finish handler, reset failures on a response below 500 (add a public recordSuccess on CircuitBreaker that closes from HALF_OPEN and zeroes failures). Do not count a 503 the route sent as a typed refusal: skip when res.locals.breakerIgnore is set, and set it in stream.ts's GATEWAY_UNAVAILABLE branch.
test: circuitBreaker middleware test: send 10 responses of 503 through the middleware, then 1 of 200. The failure count resets, and a following GET on /api/ana-ri/agent-activity is not refused with circuit_open.
observed: Right after the turn, GET /api/ana-ri/agent-activity and GET /api/ana-ri/live-drive/state return 503 {"error":"Service ai-service is temporarily unavailable","status":"circuit_open","retry_after":10}. The Progress panel shows 'Background: Couldn't read the background queue. Retry'. The circuit is shared across users, so one tester's failed AnA turns break another user's background-queue and live-drive reads.

title: Forced sign-out lands on Sign in with no explanation, and the sign-in page ignores dark mode
root: Not reproduced in the UI; the frequent sign-outs come from a shared account on a shared dev server. Code: the client maps only SESSION_IDLE, SESSION_LIFETIME and SESSION_SUPERSEDED to a sign-in notice (client/src/utils/sessionEnd.ts:15). The device-limit path sends SESSION_SUPERSEDED and is explained. The server also answers 401 code 'SESSION_ENDED' for a revoked token or a session ended by account standing (server/middleware/auth.ts:212,220; server/auth.ts:164,188). sessionEndReasonOf returns null for that code, so Concept2CureLogin.tsx:201 has no reason to show. Dark mode is applied by the v2 shell only (V2App.tsx:147 and around :1264, on body), so the sign-in page, outside the shell, renders light.
fix: Add SESSION_ENDED: 'ended' to CODES and to the SessionEndReason union and takeSignOutReason, with a sign-in notice: 'Your session ended. Sign in again.' In Concept2CureLogin, read the c2c-v2-prefs dark flag (try/catch) and apply the same dark marker the shell uses.
